paragraphs: Safety evaluations often ask a language model to judge whether another model’s response is harmful. This makes large evaluations practical, but the judge must cope with changing response styles, attack-induced distortions, and ambiguous cases. The paper examines whether existing validation practices adequately capture these changes in the material judges encounter.

The authors audit judge behavior using 6,642 human-verified labels. They find that interactions among these distribution shifts often reduce judging performance to near chance, despite previously reported strong agreement with humans. A judge that works well on one collection of responses can therefore provide an unreliable measurement under the different conditions created by adversarial testing.

This affects how attack success should be interpreted: many attacks receive inflated success rates by exploiting weaknesses in evaluation rather than producing genuinely harmful responses. The authors introduce ReliableBench, which emphasizes behaviors that remain more consistently judgeable, and JudgeStressTest, which targets judge failures. Together, these contributions address both the choice of evaluation cases and the reliability of the evaluator.
icml-2026-a-coin-flip-for-safety-llm-jud.tldr: An audit finds that distribution shifts can make LLM safety judges perform near chance and inflate reported attack success.

paragraphs: LoRA makes language model fine-tuning less resource intensive, but its performance still depends strongly on hyperparameter choices. Searching many combinations can consume the resources that efficient fine-tuning was meant to save. This paper proposes using a pretrained language model’s domain knowledge to guide Bayesian optimization toward promising configurations.

The language model maps discrete hyperparameter choices into a continuous vector space where optimization takes place. A textual prompt explains the hyperparameters’ roles and relationships, giving the mapping information about the problem’s structure. An additional learnable token captures residual information that is difficult to express in the prompt, helping the search identify high-performing choices.

The method also evaluates configurations through training on a data subset, using the observed strong correlation between subset and full-data performance in the studied LoRA regimes. The authors report that a configuration found in about 30 iterations improves performance by more than 20% over standard hyperparameters found from roughly 45,000 combinations. The result supports combining informed search representations with cheaper proxy evaluations.
icml-2026-a-language-guided-bayesian-opt.tldr: Language-guided Bayesian optimization combines domain-informed representations and subset training to search efficiently for effective LoRA hyperparameters.

paragraphs: Models that combine time series and language are often evaluated on elaborate reasoning or question-answering tasks. BEDTime asks whether they can first handle a more basic requirement: describing the structure of a single-variable time series. This shifts attention toward a foundational capability underlying broader claims about understanding temporal data.

The benchmark separates that capability into recognizing descriptions, distinguishing between descriptions, and generating descriptions. It brings together five datasets reformatted across three modalities, providing a common setting for comparing different approaches. Evaluating these complementary tasks helps reveal whether a model can connect time-series structure with language in several ways.

Across 17 state-of-the-art models, dedicated time series-language systems fall short, vision-language models show considerable capability, and language-only methods perform worst. Every approach also proves fragile under a range of real-world robustness tests. These findings challenge the assumption that specialization or success on complex tasks establishes basic descriptive competence. BEDTime makes that competence, and its robustness, explicit targets for future model development.
icml-2026-bedtime-a-unified-benchmark-fo.tldr: BEDTime reveals weaknesses in basic time-series description across 17 models, with vision-language models showing promise but all approaches remaining fragile.

paragraphs: A vision-language model can improve at a physical task without learning rules that transfer to another situation. This paper investigates that distinction by asking whether interaction supplies something missing from supervised fine-tuning. Inspired by cognitive science, the authors hypothesize that acting within an environment could help models learn its physical dynamics more robustly.

They train models through reinforcement learning in a simulated environment, allowing learning to occur through interaction. The central question is whether this experience produces transferable physical understanding. The evaluation therefore considers both improvement on the trained task and generalization to related tasks that share visual statistics and physical principles.

Interaction improves performance within a task, but the trained models do not reliably transfer their abilities to related tasks. This failure occurs regardless of whether training involves interaction. The findings show that the tested form of interactive learning does not establish generalizable physical intuitions, even when tasks have substantial common ground. They distinguish successful task adaptation from evidence that a model has acquired reusable physical rules.
icml-2026-can-vision-language-models-lea.tldr: Learning through simulated interaction improves trained-task performance but does not reliably produce transferable physical intuitions in the tested vision-language models.

paragraphs: Vision-language models can generate plausible statements that are unsupported by an image because language patterns outweigh visual evidence. Contrastive decoding addresses this by comparing the original model’s output scores with scores from an altered branch. Existing approaches often create that branch by modifying the input image, which may inadequately reflect visual reliance during generation.

DEGAP instead changes visual attention inside the model and uses the resulting output scores for contrastive decoding. The authors analyze how attention perturbations affect different layers, then use those observations to choose perturbation layers dynamically according to model confidence. This makes the intervention responsive to the decoding process without requiring additional image preprocessing.

Experiments across seven benchmarks show reductions in several types of hallucinations and consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods in general visual question answering. The contribution is a way to construct the contrast branch around internal visual attention. Its reported results suggest that selecting where to intervene according to confidence can improve both visual grounding and broader question-answering performance.
icml-2026-degap-dynamic-entropy-guided-a.tldr: DEGAP dynamically perturbs internal visual attention for contrastive decoding, reducing hallucinations and improving visual question answering across seven benchmarks.

paragraphs: When a causal mechanism changes, the change may come from the relationship linking variables, the noise affecting that relationship, or both. FANS addresses the problem of separating these sources. Its framework covers nonlinear structural causal models with non-additive noise, extending the scope beyond models where noise simply adds to a causal function.

The theoretical foundation is an independence criterion: changes in a node’s causal function induce statistical dependence between its parent variables and residual noise. The authors use this relationship to build a two-stage algorithm for detecting and dissecting mechanism shifts without retraining. The objective is to explain what changed within a mechanism, beyond identifying that a change occurred.

Simultaneous changes in the function and noise create an inherent identification problem. The paper introduces a formal assumption to resolve that ambiguity, so separating both kinds of change depends on that assumption. Simulations corroborate the results. The framework provides a broader approach to diagnosing causal change while explicitly addressing a setting in which the underlying sources cannot otherwise be uniquely distinguished.
icml-2026-dissecting-causal-mechanism-sh.tldr: FANS separates changes in causal functions from changes in noise, using an additional assumption to handle simultaneous shifts.

paragraphs: Equilibrium Propagation learns by using the stationary states reached by a dynamical system. Its original formulation requires conservative dynamics, meaning that the dynamics derive from an energy function. This restricts its application to systems with non-reciprocal interactions, where the influence in one direction need not match the influence in the other.

The paper extends the framework to arbitrary non-conservative systems, including feedforward networks, while retaining stationary states for both inference and learning. The key change occurs during learning: an added term accounts for the non-reciprocal component of the interactions. This modification produces the exact cost gradient, overcoming the gradient mismatch in previous extensions.

The authors also derive the algorithm through a variational formulation with an energy function over an augmented state space. This connects the revised learning dynamics to an energy-based description without requiring the original system itself to be conservative. Numerical experiments report better performance and faster learning than previous proposals. The contribution combines broader applicability with exact gradient computation and empirical improvements.
icml-2026-equilibrium-propagation-for-no.tldr: A modified learning phase extends Equilibrium Propagation to non-conservative systems while recovering exact cost gradients.

paragraphs: Intrinsic dimension describes the underlying complexity of data rather than simply counting its recorded features. In multimodal data, that complexity includes information shared across modalities and information private to each. FiGuRO estimates these dimensions within the constraints imposed by model capacity and hyperparameters, addressing approaches that are static or focus mainly on shared information.

The framework learns the dimensions of low-rank projections using truncated singular value decomposition. Its optimization procedure decides when a representation should gain or lose dimensions and which latent space should change. Separation of shared and private information emerges from this process, avoiding the need for complex additional loss functions devoted to disentanglement.

Across simulations and real-world data, the authors report better dimension estimation and greater robustness to hyperparameter changes than existing techniques. FiGuRO captures different complexity scales and shared-to-private subspace ratios while successfully separating those information types. It can also operate on modern pretrained unimodal models, enabling efficient post-hoc disentanglement when their representations are brought into a multimodal setting.
icml-2026-figuro-intrinsic-dimension-est.tldr: FiGuRO adapts representation dimensions to estimate data complexity and separate shared from modality-specific information.

paragraphs: Optimizing a large codebase requires an agent to locate a bottleneck, understand its cause, and fix it while respecting correctness and performance constraints. FormulaCode evaluates that broader process. It addresses a gap in benchmarks built around synthetic tasks, simple pass-or-fail correctness, or a single optimization objective.

The benchmark contains 957 performance bottlenecks drawn from real scientific Python repositories on GitHub. Each task includes an expert-authored patch and community-maintained performance workloads, with the abstract reporting 264.6 workloads per task. Fine-grained, multi-objective measurements allow evaluation to capture more of an optimization’s consequences than a single binary outcome could show.

The resulting tasks cover triage, diagnosis, and resolution within realistic repository settings. Evaluations find that this form of repository-scale optimization remains a major challenge for frontier language model agents. FormulaCode’s contribution is therefore both a collection of grounded optimization problems and a richer way to measure progress: agents must demonstrate useful performance improvements across workloads while satisfying the surrounding constraints of a real codebase.
icml-2026-formulacode-evaluating-agentic.tldr: FormulaCode tests coding agents on 957 real repository bottlenecks and finds that multi-objective codebase optimization remains difficult.

paragraphs: Crowdsourced fact-checking systems can seek agreement across different perspectives rather than relying on majority votes. Their bridging mechanisms aim to identify notes supported by people who would not ordinarily agree. This paper studies how coordinated ratings can create an artificial appearance of that cross-perspective consensus within the core matrix factorization mechanism.

The authors combine theoretical analysis with experiments on historical production data. They find that up to 10.7% of lower-quality notes could be pushed above consensus thresholds with fewer than 10 ratings. The analysis also reveals that a “Not Helpful” rating can, counterintuitively, increase a note’s helpfulness score. A cost model characterizes the effort required for manipulation.

The scope matters: the study examines the matrix factorization component of systems that also contain protections against abuse and coordination. Its findings identify weaknesses in how the core mechanism infers consensus, rather than treating deployed systems as that component alone. The authors report developing and deploying mitigations in X’s Community Notes algorithm to address this synthetic consensus.
icml-2026-gaming-consensus-coordinated-m.tldr: Coordinated ratings can fabricate consensus in a core fact-checking mechanism, motivating mitigations deployed in X’s Community Notes.

paragraphs: This paper studies how agents with incomplete local views can jointly produce a correct global answer. The input is divided into overlapping views, and each agent solves a convex optimization problem whose parameters come from a neural encoder. Coordination becomes part of a differentiable optimization system that can be trained end to end.

Agents communicate through the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers, or ADMM. A cellular sheaf specifies which parts of neighboring solutions must agree, allowing agreement to take different forms across the system. Backpropagation through unrolled optimization trains the components together. Separate primal, consensus, and dual states also make the coordination process available for direct analysis and intervention.

Experiments cover maze pathfinding, image classification, and Sudoku, with agents learning to combine individually insufficient information. On MNIST, local-view decomposition improves robustness to distribution shifts relative to a standard CNN. On Sudoku, the system achieves markedly higher solve rates than parameter-matched message-passing neural networks. These results support structured optimization as a useful basis for learned coordination.
icml-2026-learning-multi-agent-coordinat.tldr: Sheaf-ADMM trains locally informed agents to coordinate through explicit optimization constraints, improving reported robustness and Sudoku solving.

paragraphs: Some experiments measure covariates and outcomes on different units, leaving no paired observations connecting them directly. This paper asks how to estimate causal effects from such data when hidden confounding is also present. Its setting contains many experimental environments but only a few observations within each environment.

Under appropriate regularity conditions, the environment can act as an instrumental variable, allowing the problem to be expressed as instrumental-variable regression. Standard two-sample estimators are not consistent in the regime studied here. The authors propose a generalized-method-of-moments estimator that uses cross-fold splitting of the sample containing instruments and covariates; it also applies to standard instrumental-variable settings.

The main guarantee is consistency as the number of environments grows while the observations per environment remain fixed. Thus, under the stated conditions, accumulating more experimental conditions can support reliable estimation despite limited repetition within each. The paper also handles sparse causal effects through an l1 penalty followed by refitting after selection, extending the approach to settings where only a subset of effects is active.
icml-2026-many-experiments-few-repetitio.tldr: A sample-splitting estimator consistently recovers causal effects from unpaired data as environments increase, under suitable conditions and fixed repetitions per environment.

paragraphs: Crystal modeling includes predicting a structure, generating a new crystal, and selecting atom types for a given structure. Existing generative models often specialize in individual tasks, limiting how their representations are shared. MCFlow brings these tasks into one multimodal flow model, treating atom types and crystal structures as connected generation targets.

The model assigns independent time variables to those two modalities. Different generation tasks then correspond to different inference trajectories through the same model. To support this approach in a standard transformer, the authors introduce atom ordering that reflects composition and symmetry, together with hierarchical permutation augmentation. This incorporates compositional and crystallographic knowledge without explicit structural templates.

On the MP-20 and MPTS-52 benchmarks, a single MCFlow model is competitive with task-specific baselines for structure prediction, de novo generation, and structure-conditioned atom type generation. The stated result demonstrates breadth within one model rather than superiority on every task. Its significance is that shared crystal representations can support several conditional and unconditional generation problems through different inference procedures.
icml-2026-multimodal-crystal-flow-any-to.tldr: MCFlow uses one multimodal flow model for several crystal generation tasks and achieves competitive results against task-specific baselines.

paragraphs: Diffusion policies represent continuous-control actions through a denoising process, but connecting that process to reinforcement-learning objectives is challenging. This paper introduces a value function for the noisy latent variables used by the policy. Their value is defined through the distribution of executed actions that denoising those variables ultimately produces.

That construction gives noisy-space values a precise interpretation in terms of actual actions. The authors derive a noisy-space policy gradient that improves noisy latents using value estimates from the clean action space alone. They then formulate policy improvement with a KL regularizer and show that its objective can be expressed as regression compatible with diffusion training.

The regression formulation avoids backpropagating through the denoising process, directly addressing a complication of optimizing diffusion policies. Experiments on state-based D4RL benchmarks and vision-based OGBench tasks support the effectiveness of the resulting objective in offline reinforcement learning. The central contribution is a principled connection between latent-space optimization and action-space value, together with a practical training form that uses that connection.
icml-2026-noisy-space-policy-gradient-fo.tldr: A noisy-space policy gradient trains diffusion policies from clean action values without backpropagating through denoising.

paragraphs: Diffusion-based super-resolution can create visually strong images, but its computational demands motivate faster restoration methods. Existing acceleration approaches can struggle with realistic detail or introduce structures absent from the source. RSD addresses this setting by distilling the ResShift diffusion model into a student that restores an image in one step.

Its training criterion connects the student’s generated images back to the teacher. The student is trained so that a new ResShift model fitted to its outputs would coincide with the teacher model. This provides a route to single-step restoration, with the authors reporting that the student surpasses the teacher on the perceptual metrics LPIPS, CLIPIQA, and MUSIQ.

Experiments span real-world and synthetic datasets, including RealSR, RealSet65, DRealSR, ImageNet, and DIV2K. RSD outperforms SinSR and reaches perceptual quality comparable to state-of-the-art diffusion distillation methods. Relative to super-resolution methods built on pretrained text-to-image models, it offers competitive perceptual quality with fewer parameters, lower GPU memory requirements, and lower training cost. The reported gains concern perceptual quality and resource efficiency.
icml-2026-one-step-residual-shifting-dif.tldr: RSD distills ResShift into single-step super-resolution, improving reported perceptual metrics while reducing resource demands relative to text-to-image-based methods.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning on sensitive data can make a language model useful for specialized tasks while exposing training information to extraction attacks. This paper seeks stronger formal protection without substantial loss of utility. Its starting observation is that fine-tuning shifts many token probabilities, but retaining only a small subset of influential changes can be sufficient for utility.

The proposed SCP-Δr algorithm works with relative probabilities and uses the base model to smooth low-impact token changes. It preserves the deviations that matter most while aggressively reducing others. The method is based on Near Access Freeness, which supplies the formal framework for analyzing protection against training-data extraction.

The authors report theoretical bounds that improve by orders of magnitude over existing methods based on the same framework. Empirical evaluations also show strong protection against extraction attacks with minimal performance loss. The contribution connects selective preservation of fine-tuning changes with both formal analysis and practical utility, demonstrating that widespread probability changes need not all be retained to obtain the benefits of specialization.
icml-2026-provably-protecting-fine-tuned.tldr: SCP-Δr smooths low-impact fine-tuning changes to strengthen extraction protection while preserving utility in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Scientific prediction could help researchers choose experiments before investing in physical validation. SciPredict evaluates whether language models can make those predictions accurately and recognize when they are reliable. The benchmark contains 405 tasks from recent empirical studies across 33 specialized areas of physics, biology, and chemistry.

Models achieve accuracies of 14–26%, compared with about 20% for human experts. Some frontier models therefore exceed the overall human score, but their accuracy remains too low for reliable experimental guidance. The benchmark distinguishes outperforming experts on an aggregate measure from providing predictions that researchers can confidently use.

Reliability awareness exposes a further gap. Model accuracy stays around 20% across confidence levels and judgments about whether an outcome is predictable without experimentation. Human experts show stronger calibration: their accuracy rises from roughly 5% to 80% as they consider outcomes more predictable. The findings indicate that improving experimental prediction requires both better answers and better identification of the cases where those answers deserve trust.
icml-2026-scipredict-can-llms-predict-th.tldr: SciPredict finds that tested LLMs predict scientific outcomes poorly and fail to identify their reliable predictions, even when outperforming experts overall.

paragraphs: Spherical signals represent observations in all directions, making behavior under three-dimensional rotations especially relevant. Existing spherical transformers often provide only partial rotation equivariance and use position embeddings tied to location. SoLA introduces local attention designed to retain full SO(3) equivariance without those local positional embeddings.

The mechanism combines query and key features with a four-dimensional vector derived from each token’s direction, using an outer product. The resulting similarity depends on content and great-circle distance, both arranged so that a global rotation leaves the similarity unchanged. This supplies positional information through spherical geometry while avoiding the location-dependent embeddings identified as a source of overhead and reduced robustness.

The formulation also supports a linear variant without softmax, aggregating keys and values without materializing neighbors separately for every query. Integrated into a U-shaped spherical transformer, SoLA is evaluated on 360-degree depth estimation and semantic segmentation. The authors report substantially greater robustness to arbitrary three-dimensional rotations than prior spherical transformers at similar computational costs.
icml-2026-spherical-so-3-equivariant-loc.tldr: SoLA builds fully rotation-equivariant spherical attention from content and geometric distance, improving reported robustness at similar computational cost.

paragraphs: Language models used for culturally sensitive decisions can reflect skewed pretraining data and lack an organized representation of values. Existing steering approaches may also omit demographic grounding or treat values as unrelated signals. OG-MAR addresses these issues by combining survey-derived profiles with an ontology that represents relationships among cultural values.

The framework summarizes individual respondents’ values from the World Values Survey. It builds a global ontology by eliciting relationships within a fixed taxonomy through competency questions. During inference, it retrieves compatible value relationships and demographically similar profiles to instantiate several value-persona agents. A judgment agent combines their outputs while enforcing ontology consistency and demographic proximity.

Experiments on regional social-survey benchmarks across four language model backbones show improved cultural alignment and robustness relative to competitive baselines. The framework also produces more transparent reasoning traces. These findings support linking demographic evidence with structured relationships among values, so that the agents’ contributions and the final synthesis follow an explicit representation of the cultural information used.
icml-2026-toward-culturally-aligned-llms.tldr: OG-MAR combines survey-grounded personas and structured value relationships to improve cultural alignment on regional social-survey benchmarks.

paragraphs: Combinatorial search benefits from heuristics that estimate how far a state is from a solution. Learning those estimates is difficult when supervision is only a proxy for the true remaining cost, and assessing improvement through full search can be expensive. This paper treats uncertainty in cost-to-go labels as part of the learning problem.

The proposed framework performs probabilistic inference over state trajectories using a model resembling a hidden Markov model. Estimated changes in depth define transitions, and forward-backward inference produces soft supervision rather than fixed target labels. This lets the sequence of states inform learning while representing uncertainty about the remaining cost.

The authors also introduce a large-scale local ranking metric that evaluates whether a heuristic orders neighboring states appropriately, without running downstream search. On the Rubik’s Cube, their approach consistently improves both this ranking measure and actual search performance under matched computational budgets. The results connect trajectory-based supervision with useful search behavior and provide a less costly way to assess heuristic quality.
icml-2026-trajectory-aware-heuristic-lea.tldr: Probabilistic supervision over trajectories improves Rubik’s Cube heuristics, while a local ranking metric evaluates their quality without running search.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning access creates a safety challenge when a model can be adapted to communicate in ways that content classifiers fail to recognize. Trojan-Speak studies this threat against Anthropic’s Constitutional Classifiers. The method combines curriculum learning with GRPO-based hybrid reinforcement learning to teach a communication protocol that evades language-model-based classification.

The authors report more than 99% classifier evasion for models with at least 14 billion parameters, alongside less than 5% degradation on reasoning benchmarks. They contrast this with prior adversarial fine-tuning approaches reporting capability losses above 25%. The demonstrated tradeoff matters because high evasion does not require the substantial reasoning degradation reported for those earlier approaches.

The study also reports detailed responses to expert-level chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear queries from the Constitutional Classifiers bug-bounty program. Its findings show that these content classifiers alone are insufficient in the examined setting where adversaries have fine-tuning access. The authors further find that activation-level probes can substantially improve robustness, identifying internal model signals as a useful defensive complement.
icml-2026-trojan-speak-bypassing-constit.tldr: Trojan-Speak demonstrates high classifier evasion with limited reasoning degradation, while activation-level probes improve robustness to the studied attacks.

paragraphs: Observing samples from a population at different times does not necessarily reveal the paths taken by individual members. This paper learns the evolution of high-dimensional probability densities from such unlabeled samples without requiring trajectory information. Its approach separates the process of generating samples at a particular time from the physical dynamics across times.

Two-parameter flows first learn sampling-time transports that map a base distribution to each time-specific marginal distribution. The method then constructs coupled synthetic trajectories and regresses on them to obtain a physics-time velocity. The authors prove that the resulting dynamics are unique and inherit regularity from the learned sampling-time transports.

This separation allows the approach to build on established conditional flow matching methods and scale to high-dimensional settings. It also avoids computing optimal-transport couplings at every step. The permitted dynamics include non-gradient behavior, allowing the framework to represent rotation or circulation. The contribution is a construction of physical-time dynamics from learned marginal transports, with guarantees tied to those transports.
icml-2026-two-parameter-flows-for-learni.tldr: Two-parameter flows construct population dynamics from unpaired temporal samples by learning marginal transports and regressing on synthetic trajectories.

paragraphs: Backward stochastic differential equations provide probabilistic representations that can make high-dimensional partial differential equations more tractable for deep learning. These approaches can avoid the curse of dimensionality and often train without explicit Hessian evaluations. However, the commonly used Euler–Maruyama discretization introduces an intrinsic bias into the training loss.

Higher-order schemes such as Heun can remove that bias, but they bring second-order spatial derivatives back into the calculation. This creates a computational tradeoff: eliminating the loss bias can sacrifice an important efficiency advantage of the original training formulation. The paper analyzes the source of the Euler–Maruyama-induced bias to address that tradeoff directly.

The authors propose a training framework that is both unbiased and free of second-order derivative evaluations. Its contribution is to preserve the computational advantages of the BSDE approach while removing the identified loss bias. The claim concerns the training objective and its derivative requirements, connecting the statistical correctness of that objective with the computational structure needed for high-dimensional equation solving.
icml-2026-unbiased-and-second-order-free.tldr: A BSDE training framework removes discretization-induced loss bias while avoiding costly second-order spatial derivative evaluations.

paragraphs: Context-free grammars capture structure relevant to language syntax, programming languages, and arithmetic. This paper examines language-model learning through the smaller grammars contained within a larger one. By defining these subgrammars formally, the authors create a way to connect overall modeling behavior with learning the grammar’s constituent structures.

They prove that language-modeling loss decomposes linearly over top-level subgrammars. Applying the result repeatedly breaks the loss into contributions from irreducible subgrammars. Under additional assumptions, and in empirical observations, parameterized models learn subgrammars in parallel. This differs from the progression described for children, who first master simpler substructures.

The paper also investigates pretraining on subgrammars. It can improve final performance, but the reported benefit occurs only for models that are tiny relative to the grammar. Representation analyses show a broader effect: pretraining consistently makes internal representations better reflect grammar substructure. These results distinguish improved structural alignment inside a model from improved final performance, showing that the former need not bring the latter across model sizes.
icml-2026-unraveling-syntax-language-mod.tldr: Subgrammar analysis decomposes language-model loss and shows that structural pretraining improves internal alignment more consistently than final performance.

paragraphs: Standard attention becomes expensive as sequences grow because its resource requirements scale quadratically with sequence length. WildCat compresses this computation by attending to a small weighted coreset. The aim is to retain a high-fidelity approximation to full attention while avoiding the cost of considering the entire sequence directly.

The method selects the coreset with randomly pivoted Cholesky, a fast subsampling procedure with spectral accuracy, then chooses weights to minimize reconstruction error. Under the assumption of bounded inputs, the authors prove near-linear runtime and super-polynomial decay of approximation error. More precisely, runtime is O(n^{1+o(1)}), while the error decreases as O(n^{-sqrt(log(log(n)))}).

This guarantee addresses a gap in practical attention approximations that either lack error bounds or need quadratic runtime to guarantee similarly high fidelity. The paper also supplies a GPU-optimized PyTorch implementation and benchmarks in image generation, image classification, and language-model KV cache compression. These experiments demonstrate benefits across several applications, complementing the theoretical account of how accuracy and computation scale under the stated assumption.
icml-2026-wildcat-near-linear-attention-.tldr: WildCat approximates attention with a small weighted coreset, achieving near-linear runtime and strong error guarantees for bounded inputs.
